issue_context.title: Generated web worker script tries to import css file on development
issue_context.body:
<!---
Thanks for filing an issue 😄 ! Before you submit, please read the following:

Search open/closed issues before submitting since someone might have asked the same thing before!
-->

# 🐛 bug report

I am trying to set up a project with `tailwindcss` and `threads`, which provides a thin wrapper on top of native web worker.

On development environment with `parcel serve`, worker script has an unexpected `importScript('./app_name.[hash].css')` which crashes the worker thread. `parcel build` does not have this issue.


## 🎛 Configuration (.babelrc, package.json, cli command)

<!--- If describing a bug, tell us what your babel configuration looks like -->

https://github.com/quangta93/parcel-tailwindcss-threads

## 🤔 Expected Behavior

<!--- Tell us what should happen -->

Worker script built on development should not include style files. Scripts generated on development and production should have the same behaviors.

## 😯 Current Behavior

<!--- Tell us what happens instead of the expected behavior -->

On development environment with `parcel serve`, worker script has an unexpected `importScript('./app_name.[hash].css')` which crashes the worker thread. `parcel build` does not have this issue.

<!--- If you are seeing an error, please include the full error message and stack trace -->
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2924390/84930539-13629700-b097-11ea-82eb-dc98476daef1.png)


## 💁 Possible Solution

<!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix/reason for the bug -->
Native web worker works fine with `tailwindcss`. It's the specific combination of `tailwindcss` (or maybe just postcss) with `threads` (which hijacks the native Worker class).

## 🔦 Context

<!--- How has this issue affected you? What are you trying to accomplish? -->

<!--- Providing context helps us come up with a solution that is most useful in the real world -->
A common scenario is to use web worker to handle I/O and heavy computation. I am utilizing `threads` and its observable pattern for this purpose. `tailwindcss` is for building UI components.

## 💻 Code Sample

<!-- Please provide a code repository, gist, code snippet or sample files to reproduce the issue -->
https://github.com/quangta93/parcel-tailwindcss-threads

## 🌍 Your Environment

<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->

| Software         | Version(s) |
| ---------------- | ---------- |
| Parcel           |2.0.0-alpha.3.2|
| Node             |v12.14.1|
| npm/Yarn         |1.12.0|
| Operating System |Windows 10|

<!-- Love parcel? Please consider supporting our collective:
👉  https://opencollective.com/parcel/donate -->
comments: Edit: The issue is only observed when using typescript!
Same here. Even trying to import a JSON file into the worker is causing CSS import to be added.
After bundling, the CSS bundle is a sibling of both the main JS bundle (correct) and the worker bundle (wrong), and only if worker & main bundle are sharing JS assets. And indeed only with `serve`

review_comments: First problem in React Spectrum (has a test case)

Second problem in React Spectrum (couldn't find a test case because this is likely caused by Devon's custom plugins, not sure if this is the correct solution)

https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/parcel-4884-repro-1/run.sh.png
https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/parcel-4884-repro-1/run.sh.png
I think it's somehow caused by the `isIsolated:true` `client` dependency of `Checkbox.mdx`
The worker problem is solved by using "ChainedSet" (so that adding a sibling bundle for a parent doesn't propagate down, only adding a sibling to a child node should add it to the ancestry as well)
The more we add to this, the more I think maybe it should be part of the graph?
